tei:titleStmt.tei:title: הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ
Hashkivenu, rhymed translation by Alice Lucas (1898)

tei:div.tei:head: Hashkivenu, rhymed translation by Alice Lucas (1898)

tei:lg.tei:l: Cause us, our Father, to lie down in peace,
And raise us up, our King, to life again;
And let us ‘neath Thy tent of peace remain.
O save us for the sake of Thy great name,
Be unto us a shield, Thou King of kings.
Shelter us in the shadow of Thy wings.
Our guardian and deliverer Thou art,
Merciful king, whom heaven and earth adore!
Guard Thou from harm and sin
With life and peace henceforth and evermore.

tei:note.tei:p: The Sefaradi version has “our Father” while the Ashkenazi version has “YHVH Eloheinu.” Most of the following however follows the Ashkenazi phrasing.

Possibly, just “dever, raav, and yagon” (pestilence, famine, and sorrow), but I’m adding the complete litany of dangers provided in the Sefaradi variation for good measure, here, which Alice Lucas has summarized. She does omit the following line, “remove the Satan (Adversary) from in front and behind us.”
By “harm and sin” I think Alice Lucas may have been looking to integrate the Sefaradi variation into the Ashkenazi phrasing.
